 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 14/03/2018, PASSED IN MVC NO.1742/2014, ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, MANGALURU, D.K., PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is directed against the judgment and award in MVC No.1742/2014 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mangaluru, D.K. on 14-3-2018, whereby, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,43,050/- on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner contended that on 14-8-2014 while he was proceeding as a rider of the motor cycle near Amtoor school, Amtoor village, Bantwal Taluk, the Qualis car bearing No.KA.19/ME-5969 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, resulting in his falling down and causing injuries to him.
He was shifted to Father Muller's Medical College Hospital, Mangalore and NC: 2023:KHC:25056 was inpatient and thereafter, he was shifted to Tejasvini Hospital, Mangalore.

During the treatment, it was found that the petitioner has sustained (i) Type III open fracture of right medial femoral condyle; (ii) fracture of inferior pubic rami with posterior wall and anterior column acetabular fracture on right side (pelvic bone); (iii) subluxated right hip (iv) comminuted fracture of the distal part of the tibia involving its articular surface at the ankle joint (pilon) with distal fibula bone and several rounds of surgeries were conducted on him.

The petitioner contended that he was inpatient for about 118 days on different spells and had to spend a sum of Rs.6,00,000/-
towards his medical expenses and he require another Rs.4,00,000/- for further treatment and as such adequate and just compensation be awarded to him.
He also contended that he was an agriculturist and real estate agent aged 43 years and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In pursuance to the notice issued, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 appeared through their counsel before the Tribunal an filed their objections statement.
4. Respondent No.1 who is the owner of the car contended that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and that there was contributory negligence.

He also contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, imaginary an untenable and the age,
income and occupation are to be proved by the petitioner.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 contended that there was no such accident as alleged by the petitioner and the involvement of the vehicle was disputed.
Inter alia, it was alleged that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and imaginary.
Further, it was contended that the terms and conditions of the policy were not complied by respondent No.1 and therefore, the liability on the respondent No.2 may be absolved.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW1 and two doctors were examined as PWs 2 and 3 and two more witness were examined on his part as
PWs 4 an 5 and Exs.P1 to P38 were marked.
Respondents have not led any evidence.

However, the copy of the insurance policy was marked as Ex.P1.
7.

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.8,43,050/- as compensation under the following heads:
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 10,000/-
 Conveyance, food and Rs. 24,000/-
 attendant  Medical expenses Rs. 6,05,850/-
 Loss of earning during Rs. 42,000/-
 treatment period  Loss of future income Rs. 1,51,200/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 10,000/-

Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager, low and not in accordance with the settled position of laws.
On issuance of notice, respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and the respondent No.1 did not appear despite service of notice.
The Tribunal records have been secured.

10. Heard the learned counsel appearing for both the sides and perused the records.
11.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC contending that subsequent to the award, petitioner continued to take treatment for the injuries sustained by him and therefore, the subsequent events taken place needs to be considered by this Court.
He contended that the petitioner had to spend more than Rs.1,50,000/- for treatment and this aspect may be considered by the Court in order to arrive at a just and proper conclusion.

sentences.text: The first aspect to be considered by this Court is regarding the application filed by the petitioner under order 41 Rule 27 CPC.

It is to be noted that provision of order 41 Rule 27 CPC are to be invoked by this Court only NC: 2023:KHC:25056 if appellant makes a ground that he was prevented him from producing such evidence at the time of trial and such evidence was beyond his control.
It is the discretion of the Court to invoke the provision of order 41 Rule 27 CPC and it cannot be sought as a right by the party.

If the Court comes to the conclusion that such an additional evidence is essential for the just and proper decision in the case, the Court can invoke the provision of Order 41 Rule 27 CPC.
13.

When the contention of the appellant is looked into from the above view point, it is clear that the appellant was not in possession of these documents i.e. the bills for having spent a sum of Rs.1,78,000/- towards his treatment.
It is the case of the petitioner that he has suffered permanent disability and the Doctors had given evidence before the Tribunal that there will be future medical expenses.
Therefore, the appellant has filed an application under order 41 Rule 27 CPC.

Obviously,
these documents were not in possession of the appellant at the NC: 2023:KHC:25056 time of the trial.
Secondly, the Court has to assess the just, reasonable and proper compensation on the basis of the evidence available.

When certain piece of material evidence were not in the hands of appellant,
seeking the assistance of the Court at the appellate stage to look into such evidence appears to be a valid ground which is to be allowed.

The Court has to come to a just decision in the matter and in coming to such a conclusion, the documents produced by the appellant are relevant and therefore,
the application filed under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC is hereby allowed.
The documents produced by the appellant along with the IA are taken on record.

14. A careful perusal of the documents produced by the appellant go to show that though a total bill of Rs.1,62,041/- is claimed, there appears to be certain discrepancies in these bills and it would be appropriate to take the value of these bills at Rs.1,40,000/-.

15. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant contends that the petitioner was aged about 43 years, was NC: 2023:KHC:25056 an agriculturist as evidenced by Exs.P17,18 and 19 and he was having about 64 cents of land.
It is submitted that he was also an real estate agent, but there are no documents to prove the same.
Obviously, there is no material on record to show the income of the petitioner.

As a result, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.6,000/-
per month and calculated the compensation amount.
Though the conclusion of the Tribunal to adopt the notional income cannot be disputed, the amount of the notional income appears to be incorrect.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of the disputes before the Lok Adalat prescribe the notional income of Rs.8,500/- for the year 2014.

In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are held to be acceptable on the ground that they are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is accepted as Rs.8,500/- per month.

sentences.text: The PW2 Dr. Mahabala Shetty, has stated in his evidence that there are various restrictions of the movement suffered by the petitioner and the cumulative effect of such restrictions of the movement account for 44% of the disability to the right lower limb.
He has stated that there are several surgical interventions need to be done and implants may have to be removed.
The PW2 has rightly spoken about the physical disability of the right lower limb, but not about either the functional disability or whole body disability.
In medical parlance, there is no such whole body disability which can be inferred from the physical disability of a limb.
It is only a fiction which has been adopted in order to ascertain the cumulative effect of the physical disability of the limb for the purpose of convenience.
Therefore, it appears that the assessment of the disability by PW2 is proper and correct.
17. The functional disability of the petitioner has to be determined by the Tribunal/court.

Assessment of the functional disability is in the domain of the Tribunal, but - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:25056 not in the domain of a Medical Expert, for, he will not have any access to the information or proof in respect of the avocation of the petitioner.

Under these circumstances, when we juxtapose the avocation of the petitioner with that of the physical disability of the right lower limb to the extent of 44%, it is evident that the conventional formula of 1/3rd to the limb being taken as functional disability cannot be accepted.

Under these circumstances, it is evident that it would be difficult for the petitioner to continue his avocation as an agriculturist and therefore, this Court holds that the functional disability of the petitioner at 24%.

18. In view of the above conclusions, the loss of future income is calculated as: Rs.8,500/- x 12 x 14 x 24% =3,42,720/-.
19.
The records reveal that the petitioner was inpatient for a period of 117 days and even subsequent to the judgment, the petitioner has undergone treatment for about 18 days.
Under these circumstances, it can be safely be said that he could not resume his activities atleast for a - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:25056 period of 7 months as held by the Tribunal.

Hence, a sum of Rs.59,500/-
(8,500x 7) is awarded under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period'.

20. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of 'pain and sufferings' and in view of the gravity of the injury as well as there is three factures, a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded to him under the head of 'pain and sufferings'.

21. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.24,000/- under the head of 'conveyance, food and attendant charges' which appears to be on the lower side when compared to the period of treatment and therefore, a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded under this head.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.6,05,850/- towards the medical expenses and this Court by virtue of allowing the application filed under order 41 Rule 27 of CPC allowed the additional medical bills to be produced which amounts for a sum of Rs.1,40,000/- and therefore,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:25056 a sum of Rs.7,45,850/- has to be awarded under the head of 'medical expenses'.
23. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of 'loss of amenities' which obviously is on the lower side.
The petitioner has to carry the brunt of injuries in his rest of life and therefore, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under the head of 'loss of amenities in life'.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.13,08,070/-, under the following heads:
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 60,000/-
 Conveyance, food and attendant Rs. 60,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 7,45,850/-
 Loss of earning during treatment Rs. 59,500/-
 period  Loss of future income Rs. 3,42,720/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-

Total Rs.13,08,070/-
 Less: Awarded by Tribunal Rs. 8,43,050/-
Enhancement Rs. 4,65,020/-
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,65,020/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest.

Hence,
the following:
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:25056 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.4,65,020/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a, from the date of petition till its realization.
(iii) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with interest within six weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
